title: Make your agent ask before it spends money
summary: Esra Kadah built a dispatch assistant for a made-up repair company that books technicians on its own but pauses for approval before ordering paid parts.
agent_role: The agent answers dispatcher questions, looks up work orders and schedules technician visits by itself. When it wants to order a part, it stops and a person taps Approve or Decline.
outcome: The author reports the approval flow works in the demo after she found and filed a fix for a bug in the Genkit Dart library.
what_they_did: Esra Kadah built a dispatch assistant for an invented field service company, all in the Dart language. A dispatcher types requests like checking a work order or ordering a heating element. The agent can look up and book visits freely. Ordering a part costs money, so it waits for a person's approval in a phone or web app.
how_it_went: She says lookups and bookings worked, but approving an order first failed with a 'tool not found' error. She traced it to a library bug, filed it upstream with a fix, and used a small workaround until it ships.
worth_knowing: Pending approvals are kept in memory, which suits a one-server demo; a restart forgets them, so real use needs a database. Each approval can only be used once, so a double tap cannot order twice.
prompt: Help me set up an assistant for [your business] that handles requests about [your work orders or bookings]. It may look things up and schedule appointments on its own. Before any action that costs money, such as ordering parts or paying a supplier, it must stop, show me exactly what it wants to do and the cost, and wait for me to approve or decline. If I decline, it should do nothing and tell me so. Show me your plan for the tools and approval step before building anything.

curation.rationale: A working demo of a dispatch assistant that looks up work orders, books visits and asks a human before ordering parts, with code and a real upstream bug fix. It is a made-up company and mostly a developer tutorial, so it is thin as a real-world use.
